high_level_description: Wordless nineteenth-century Imagerie d’Épinal popular-print illustration: a sandboxed traveling theatre on the left submits one shape-specific request through the only inspection hatch of a local workshop, where a custodian alone controls its acceptance; bold black contours, flat hand-stenciled colors, frontal storytelling, strictly no text or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A frontal cutaway divides an open Vosges village square on the left from a protected lime-plastered workshop on the right. One thick masonry wall runs continuously from top to bottom between them, with a single small aperture at waist height. The exterior ground and interior plank floor meet the wall but never cross it. Every surface remains free of letters, numbers, captions, signs, symbols, and directional marks.

elements.desc: Compact traveling puppet theatre representing the sandboxed application, built from blue-painted wood with vermilion curtains, yellow wheels, a closed rear cabinet, and one small dispensing cup. It remains entirely outside the workshop wall; its two articulated wooden hands are empty after submitting the single request and cannot reach the protected room.

Single circular inspection hatch with its featured request token inside, treated as one unified brass chamber set through the wall. The ivory token has one asymmetric three-lobed profile that fits the matching cradle exactly. A closed exterior grille blocks the theatre, while one short decision lever exists only on the workshop side.

Local workshop custodian with medium-brown skin, short black curls, a blue work blouse, ochre apron, dark trousers, and red clogs. She stands fully inside with a calm attentive expression, compares the token against a small wooden gauge, and keeps her right hand on the hatch lever while the other hand remains visible.

Protected local cabinet fixed high on the workshop wall, made from dark blue wood with a closed brass latch and a small glazed panel revealing three unmarked ivory jars. It has no opening toward the square, no connection to the traveling theatre, and no duplicate lever accessible from outside the room.
